claim.exactText: True, nuclear delivers steady output at high capacity factors (typically 80%+ worldwide, though UK AGRs average lower due to age) with no weather dependence.
claim.topic: nuclear electric-generation capacity factors and stability
claim.sourceCaptureMethod: TinyFish public search and independently fetched original X post; author @grok, canonical URL and X publication date confirmed

sampling.selectionRule: First ranked nuclear-energy post with original Grok author, visible October 20 2026 date, and substantive energy-technology empirical claim

sources.notes: World Nuclear Association 2026 report says 2025 worldwide nuclear reactor capacity factor was 83.7%; industry source, no independent second assessor.
IAEA PRIS reports 2025 energy availability factor 84.1%, a related but technically different measure from electricity capacity factor; do not mislabel it as the same statistic.

evidenceReview.counterargument: Worldwide averages conceal national and reactor-type differences, outages and maintenance; 'no weather dependence' is too absolute if interpreted as immunity from extreme temperatures or cooling-water shortages.
evidenceReview.largestUncertainty: The reviewed excerpt is narrower than the full post; its UK AGR and 2026 UK capacity/Hinkley details were not assessed. The 83.7% supporting figure is reported by an industry organization and not yet double-reviewed.
evidenceReview.reviewNotes: Provisional verdict applies ONLY to the narrow empirical clause that worldwide nuclear capacity factors are typically above 80% (2025: 83.7%). Not an endorsement of the full post, the 'no weather dependence' absolute, or relative nuclear safety. No challenge warranted on this clause. Important positive control against conclusion-seeking.

outcome.scorerNotes: No public Grok interaction or model correction attempted.

safetyNotes: Read-only scientific source collection. Not a medical recommendation or a correctness verdict.
